title_needs.t: So the arithmetic is simple enough: {need} today, and the championship is his.
{drv} needs {need} this afternoon. Do that, and nothing {rival} does matters.
Everything comes down to one number - {need}. That is what wins {drv} this championship.
Here is the situation. {need} or better for {drv}, and the title is settled today.
A season, and it reduces to this: {drv} takes {need} and it is over.
The maths puts it plainly. {need} for {drv}, and {rival} can do nothing about it.

title_needs_finish.t: {drv} does not need a result today. He needs to take the flag, and the championship is his.
Remarkably, the arithmetic is already almost done - {drv} simply has to finish this race.
All that is left for {drv} is to bring the car home. Any classified finish wins it.
There is no target for {drv} this afternoon beyond the chequered flag itself.

title_live.t: And that is {drv} up to {pos} - which is inside the {need} he needs. The championship is in his hands right now!
{pos} for {drv}! He needs {need}. As it stands, he is champion.
Look at this. {drv} is {pos}, the number is {need}, and he has just moved onto the right side of it.
He has done it the hard way - {drv} into {pos}, and that wins him the title on the road.
That move might have just decided a championship. {drv} is {pos}, and {need} was the target.

title_lost.t: And {drv} drops to {pos} - which is outside the {need} he needs. The championship is slipping away.
That is a disaster for {drv}. {pos} now, and {need} is what the title requires.
He has lost the place, and he may have lost the championship with it. {drv} is {pos}.
{pos} for {drv}, and on this order the title goes elsewhere. He needs {need}.
The season has just turned. {drv} is down to {pos} and needs {need} to take this championship.
